newsitem.title: USA: Motorola sees 10 pct chip industry growth.
newsitem.headline: Motorola sees 10 pct chip industry growth.

text.p: Motorola Inc said Tuesday it expects the worldwide semiconductor industry to grow by about 10 percent in 1997 versus 1996, calling the recovery in the industry and its own chip business "very gradual".
"Our present forecast for worldwide semiconductor industry growth is about 10 percent for 1997 versus 1996," Ed Gams, head of Motorola investor relations, told analysts on a conference call.
"We continue to believe that we're going to see a very gradual recovery in the industry and our semiconductor business through 1997," he said.

Gams said the overcapacity in the semiconductor industry persists, and the company expects continued pricing pressures. He said Motorola does not expect a return to double-digit operating margins for its semiconductor business this year.
"We don't believe the operating margins will reach the 10 percent level in this business in 1997," Gams said.
Motorola said the operating margin for 1996 in its semiconductor business was 4.9 percent. The operating margin is the percent of operating profit of net sales.
The first quarter operating margin was not avaialable for the semiconductor business, but the company said its overall operating margin declined in the first quarter versus first quarter last year.
Late Monday, Motorola reported earnings of $0.53 a share including gains from the settlement of a patent suit and the sale of an investment, compared with $0.63 a share last year.
Sales were $6.642 billion, down from $6.955 billion last year. The company said the decline was largely attributable to the semiconductor business.
After years of historically high growth, the semiconductor industry posted a decline in worldwide revenues of some nine percent in 1996, Motorola said.
Motorola said it has emerged from that recession but recovery will be modest in 1997. It said its own equipment businesses continue to consume some 20 percent of its total semiconductor output.
"We continue to expect a modest rate of recovery for the industry and our semiconductor business with all the year-over-year growth in the second half of 1997," Gams said.
